info.title: FSHRMS — Auth API
info.description:
Authentication, authorisation, user/role/permission admin, and session
management for Forward Sports HRMS. Login at POST /auth/login, then click
"Authorize" and paste the access token to call protected endpoints.

tags.name: Admin — Users
tags.description: User accounts CRUD, role attach/detach, password reset, unlock, sessions. Requires `auth.users.*` / `auth.sessions.admin` permissions.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Login, refresh, logout. These three endpoints are unauthenticated.

tags.name: Sessions (self-service)
tags.description: List and revoke the caller's own active sessions. Device labels are set from the User-Agent at login and are not user-editable.

tags.name: Current user
tags.description: Identity, roles, and permissions for the authenticated user.

tags.name: Admin — Roles & Permissions
tags.description: Catalog reads, role write APIs, and the reverse permission→roles lookup. Permissions remain seed-only; roles support custom additions (HR ask: "Payroll Read-only" for an audit consultant). Requires `auth.roles.read` / `auth.roles.write` permissions.

tags.name: Users — Identity Resolver
tags.description: Authenticated-only batch lookup that returns the minimum identity fields (username, fullName, status) every chat / directory chip needs. No PII; no `auth.users.read` permission required — anyone signed in can resolve a userId to a display handle.

tags.name: Password (self-service)
tags.description: Authenticated user changes their own password. Admin reset is under /admin/users.

tags.name: Admin — Sessions
tags.description: Force-revoke a user's active session. Requires `auth.sessions.admin`.

tags.name: JWKS
tags.description: Public RSA key in JWK Set format. Used by other services to verify JWTs.

post.summary: Mint a new access + refresh pair
post.description: Rotates the refresh token. The previous refresh token is revoked atomically.

401.description: Refresh token unknown, expired, or already revoked.

post.description: Validates the current password, applies the password policy, re-hashes (bcrypt cost 12), clears the must-change-password flag, rotates the caller's session refresh token, and returns a fresh access + refresh token pair so the FE can replace its cached tokens in one round-trip — the previous 204 left the old `pwChangeRequired: true` JWT in play until the next refresh.

400.description: Old password wrong or new password fails policy.

post.description: Revokes the refresh token and the backing session row. Idempotent.

Returns an access + refresh token pair plus session id.
Failed attempts increment a counter and lock the account temporarily.

423.description: Account temporarily locked after too many failures.

get.description: Standard Spring `page`, `size`, and `sort` query params apply. All filters are independently optional and AND-combined server-side — FE no longer needs to pull the whole page and filter locally. Requires `auth.users.read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status. Omit to return all.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring against username, fullName, or email.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Exact role-code match (single role). Use the codes from /admin/roles — seeded codes are EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN (no ROLE_ prefix).

parameters.name: employeeLinked
parameters.description: Tri-state: omit to ignore, true for ESS-linked users, false for standalone.

post.description: Issues a temp password the user must change at first login. When the request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header, a re-issue of the same payload (same username, same `employeeLinked=true`) returns the existing user as 200 instead of 409 — used by the onboarding saga to make retries safe. Requires `auth.users.write`.

409.description: Username or email taken (no idempotency-key, or mismatched payload).

post.description: Clears `lockedUntil` and resets failed-login counter. Requires `auth.users.write`.

Issues a JWT for a service-account user (e.g. attendance-poller). Token is RS256-signed, identical claim shape to a login JWT plus `tokenType: "service"`. Returned once and not stored — capture it, seal it into the consumer's secret, and rotate by re-issuing. Resource servers accept it on signature + exp alone, so there is no session row, no refresh, and no revocation list. Cap is 730 days. Requires `auth.users.write`.
Adds the supplied roles. Existing roles are kept. Requires `auth.users.write`.
Forces the user to change at next login. Active sessions remain — revoke explicitly if needed. Requires `auth.users.reset`.

Idempotent. Flips status=DISABLED, revokes active sessions, emits `auth.user.deactivated`. Used by the termination saga to guarantee the disable lands even if the Kafka path is delayed, and by the admin UI "disable user" action. The optional body's `reason` flows into the session-revoke RevokeReason and the outbox event so consumers can distinguish admin disables from termination-driven ones; defaults to ADMIN_REVOKE when omitted. Requires `auth.users.write`.

Re-emits `auth.user.role_assigned` for every existing (user, role) pair. Use this once after deploying a service that needs a `role_members` projection (notification's fan-out path for HR-targeted approvals — bug #7). The events going forward already cover changes; this only seeds the snapshot. Idempotent on the consumer side. Requires `auth.users.write`.

200.description: Replay queued; response carries the count of pairs emitted.

get.description: Service-account roles (POLLER, ATTENDANCE_SVC) are excluded by default — they back machine identities and shouldn't show up in the user-assignment dropdown. Pass `includeServiceAccounts=true` from the role catalog admin screen when the full set is wanted. Requires `auth.roles.read`.

parameters.name: includeServiceAccounts
parameters.description: Include service-account roles in the response.

post.description: Code is immutable once created. Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE codes (no ROLE_ prefix). All permissions in the request must already exist in /admin/permissions. Requires `auth.roles.write`.

404.description: One of the requested permission codes is unknown.

patch.description: Null fields are left unchanged. Requires `auth.users.write`.

delete.description: Refuses if the role is system-seeded (EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN) or if any user currently holds it. Detach users first, then retry. Requires `auth.roles.write`.

409.description: Role is system-seeded or held by one or more users.

patch.description: Null fields are left unchanged. To replace permissions, send the full target set in `permissions` (not a diff). Both system-seeded and custom roles can be patched here; the `code` field is immutable. Requires `auth.roles.write`.

404.description: Role not found, or one of the requested permission codes is unknown.

get.summary: Search active users by username or full name
get.description: Case-insensitive substring match against username + fullName. ACTIVE only — DISABLED / LOCKED accounts are excluded so chat pickers don't surface ex-employees. Cap: 50 rows per call.
Returns one row per existing user id, deduped and ordered to match the input. Unknown ids are silently dropped — the resolver isn't a `findById` and won't 404. Cap: 200 ids per call.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated user ids; max 200 per call.

422.description: Too many ids in a single request.

get.description: Returns every active session for the caller, newest `lastSeenAt` first. The `current` flag marks the session backing this request.

delete.description: Revokes every active session for the caller. Pass `?except=current` to keep this session alive (e.g. "sign out everywhere else"). Returns the killed sessions so the FE can show "Signed out 3 sessions: Chrome on macOS, Safari on iOS, ..." without re-fetching the list.

parameters.name: except
parameters.description: Pass `current` to keep the calling session.

get.summary: Get the current user's profile and permissions
get.description: Use this on app boot to drive role/permission-gated UI.
Returns the current RS256 signing key. Other services cache and rotate from here.
Returns every active session row (refresh-token side). Use admin sessions DELETE to revoke a specific one. Requires `auth.sessions.admin`.

Proxies audit-service for `auth.login.success` / `auth.login.failed` / `user.locked` / `user.unlocked` events on this user. Pass `cursor` from the previous response's `nextCursor` to scroll back further than the page size. Requires `audit.read` — login history is operator-only and is not part of HR's employee timeline (V0015 doctrine). HR uses employee-service `/employees/{id}/history` for org-assignment changes.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response.

200.description: Page of login history, newest first.

502.description: audit-service is unreachable or returned an error.

get.description: One round-trip for the /admin overview tile counts. Replaces the four paginated `size=1` reads the FE used to do just to read `totalElements`. Requires `auth.users.read`.

200.description: Counts assembled in a single SQL pass.

get.description: Use the codes as the value for `@RequirePermission` and frontend gating. Requires `auth.roles.read`.

Reverse lookup — given a permission code, return the roles that grant it. Lets the roles page render "who has this?" without pulling the whole role catalog and joining client-side. Requires `auth.roles.read`.

200.description: Roles ordered by code, possibly empty.

delete.description: Revokes the session and deletes its refresh token. The corresponding access token still expires naturally (≤ 15 min). Returns the killed session so the FE can show "Revoked Chrome on macOS at 10:42" inline without re-fetching.

403.description: Session does not belong to the caller.

delete.summary: Detach a single role from a user

delete.description: Marks the session row revoked and invalidates the refresh token. Idempotent. Returns the killed session so the admin UI can show "Revoked Chrome on macOS at 10:42" inline without re-fetching the user's session list. Requires `auth.sessions.admin`.

RefreshRequest.description: Opaque refresh token returned at login or last refresh.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token. Treat as a credential — do not log.

TokenResponse.description: Access + refresh token pair. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

accessToken.description: Signed JWT (RS256). Place in the Authorization header for protected calls.

accessTokenExpiresAt.description: UTC instant the access token expires. Refresh before this to avoid 401.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token bound to the active session. Send to /auth/refresh to mint new tokens.

refreshTokenExpiresAt.description: UTC instant the refresh token expires. After this the user must log in again.

sessionId.description: Server-side session id. Used by admin endpoints to revoke the session.

mustChangePassword.description: True when HR provisioned a temporary password — UI must force a change before any other action.

PasswordChangeRequest.description: Self-service password change. Both fields required.

newPassword.description: New password. Must satisfy server-side password policy.

username.description: Username (case-sensitive). Same value used at user creation time.

password.description: Plain-text password. Sent over TLS in non-dev environments.

CreateUserRequest.description: Admin payload to create a new user account.

temporaryPassword.description: Temporary password — user is forced to change on first login.

employeeLinked.description: True when the account is linked to an employee record (ESS). Reverse linkage (auth → employee) is not stored on `users`; employee-service owns the relationship via `employees.user_id`.

roles.description: Role codes to attach immediately (no ROLE_ prefix; matches the seeded EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN).

UserDto.description: User account view — admin lists, get-by-id, and post-mutation responses.

status.description: Lifecycle status — drives whether the user can log in.

mustChangePw.description: True until the user changes their initial / reset password.

employeeLinked.description: True when linked to an employee record (ESS).

roles.description: Role codes assigned (sorted, distinct; no ROLE_ prefix).

lockedUntil.description: If non-null, account is locked until this UTC instant due to failed login attempts.

IssueServiceTokenRequest.description: Mint a long-lived JWT for a service-account user. Returned once, never stored. Rotation is admin-driven: re-issue, re-seal, restart the consumer.

ttlDays.description: Token lifetime in days. Cap is 730 (~2y) to keep `exp` as the one revocation lever we have until a denylist exists.

ServiceTokenResponse.description: Long-lived service-account JWT. Surfaced once at issue time. Auth does not store it; if lost, mint a new one and rotate the consumer's secret.

token.description: Bearer token. RS256, identical claim shape to a login JWT plus `tokenType: "service"`.

expiresAt.description: Token expiry as an ISO-8601 instant. Equal to issued-at + ttlDays.

jti.description: JWT id (jti). Useful for grepping audit logs after the fact.

AttachRolesRequest.description: Roles to attach to a user. At least one is required.

roles.description: Role codes to attach (no ROLE_ prefix; matches the seeded EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN).

PasswordResetRequest.description: Admin password reset. The user is forced to change on next login.

temporaryPassword.description: Temporary password to set on the account.

DisableUserRequest.description: Optional body for POST /admin/users/{id}/disable. The reason flows into the session-revoke RevokeReason and the auth.user.deactivated outbox event so downstream consumers can distinguish admin-initiated disables from termination-driven ones.

reason.description: Why the user is being disabled. Defaults to ADMIN_REVOKE when omitted, which is the right value for admin UI "disable user" actions and for the onboarding saga's compensation path. The termination saga passes EMPLOYEE_TERMINATED.

CreateRoleRequest.description: Admin payload to create a custom role.

code.description: Stable role code. Conventionally upper-snake-case, no ROLE_ prefix (matches the seeded EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN). Used in JWT claims and policy checks.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the admin UI.

permissions.description: Permission codes to attach immediately. Must already exist in /admin/permissions.

RoleDto.description: Role with its attached permission codes.

code.description: Stable role code used in JWT claims and policy checks. Seeded codes are EMPLOYEE | MANAGER | HR | ADMIN (no ROLE_ prefix).

system.description: True for Flyway-seeded roles — UI should hide the Delete control on these.

serviceAccount.description: True for roles that back a machine identity (POLLER, ATTENDANCE_SVC). Excluded from the default catalog response — pass `includeServiceAccounts=true` on /admin/roles to see them.

permissions.description: Permission codes the role grants (sorted, distinct).

UpdateUserRequest.description: Patch a user. All fields optional — null means "leave unchanged".

status.description: Switch account status. Use DISABLED to lock the user out without deleting them.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: Patch a role. Null fields are left unchanged. The `code` is immutable — change a role's code by creating a new role and re-assigning users (the code is part of the JWT contract).

permissions.description: Replace the role's permissions with this set. Send the full target set, not a diff. Pass null to leave permissions untouched.

UserIdentitySummary.description: Minimal user-identity row returned by the by-ids resolver. Intentionally narrow: only the fields a chat / mention / directory chip needs.

status.description: Account status. UI may grey out non-ACTIVE rows.

SessionDto.description: Refresh-token-backed session. Active when revokedAt is null and expiresAt is in the future.

deviceLabel.description: Best-effort device label parsed from the User-Agent at login.

deviceFamily.description: Coarse device family for UI icon-picking.

browser.description: Browser name + version, parsed from the User-Agent. Null when unknown.

os.description: OS name + version, parsed from the User-Agent. Null when unknown.

lastSeenAt.description: Last token refresh (≈ activity within the last 15 min).

current.description: True if this session backs the current request.

revokedAt.description: When the session was revoked. Null for active sessions.

revokedBy.description: Username that revoked the session (self for user-initiated, admin for admin revoke).

MeResponse.description: Current user identity, roles, and effective permissions.

employeeLinked.description: True when the user is linked to an employee record (ESS access).

mustChangePassword.description: True if the user must change their password before doing anything else.

roles.description: Role codes assigned to the user (no ROLE_ prefix; matches the Flyway seed).

permissions.description: Flattened, distinct permission codes from all roles.

lastLoginAt.description: Last successful login (UTC). Null on first login.

LoginHistoryEntry.description: One login-related audit event for a user.

success.description: True if the login attempt succeeded.

reason.description: Failure reason for failed/locked entries (BAD_PASSWORD, USER_DISABLED, USER_LOCKED).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, null at end.

UserStatsResponse.description: Aggregate counts over the users table — drives the /admin overview tile without paginating four times to read totalElements.

locked.description: Status = LOCKED (admin lock; failed-login lock surfaces via lockedUntil instead).

withMustChangePw.description: Users that must change their password at next login.

employeeLinked.description: Users linked to an employee record (ESS access).

standalone.description: Users not linked to any employee (system / admin / consultant).

PermissionDto.description: A single permission row from the catalog.

code.description: Stable permission code referenced from @RequirePermission and policy checks.

group.description: UI grouping for the permission catalog (server-decided so non-engineers see "Identity" instead of "auth.users.*").

description.description: 1-line plain-English explanation of what the permission allows.
description.example: Create, update, lock, and unlock user accounts.

BulkRevokeResult.description: Sessions actually killed by a bulk revoke. Empty when there was nothing to revoke.

revoked.description: Sessions revoked, in the order they were processed (newest active first).

Authorization.description: Paste the access token returned from POST /auth/login (without the 'Bearer ' prefix).
Authorization.name: Authorization
